tracks.title: Flask on the Step
tracks.genre: Motown-style sunshine soul (Detroit 1965 Hitsville lineage)
tracks.subject: a breakfast-radio host who gets up at half past three, and the sleeping wife who leaves a warm flask of tea on the front step for him every morning
tracks.caption: Motown-style sunshine soul, Detroit 1965 rhythm-section groove. Driving tambourine on the backbeat, walking Fender bass with chromatic fills, bright upright-style piano chords, baritone sax riffs and a small string section. Dry live-room recording with tape warmth, handclaps on the chorus. Male lead in a warm tenor, delivery clear and sung, girl-group trio answering the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 124 BPM, B-flat major. Bouncing, affectionate mood. No hip-hop beats, no autotune, no synth pads, no electric guitar distortion, no modern EDM drops.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - tambourine, walking bass, bright piano]

[Verse 1]
Alarm goes off at half past three
Only the streetlamps keep an eye on me
Down the stairs with my shoes in my hand
Open the door and there's a warm surprise

[Pre-Chorus]
Nobody's up but the milk float and me
And a little note, your handwriting

[Chorus]
Flask on the step, flask on the step
You're asleep, but you're looking out for me
Sugar and steam and a drive safe, love
Flask on the step, that's all I need

[Verse 2]
Seven o'clock I say good morning to town
Four hundred thousand are listening now
But the only one I'm talking to
Is the girl who's still in bed with the cat

[Chorus]
Flask on the step, flask on the step
You're asleep, but you're looking out for me
Lemon and honey and a smiley face
Flask on the step, I'll be home by three

[Bridge - drums drop to handclaps and bass]
Say it on the air, say it on the air
Good morning, darling, the tea was perfect

[Chorus]
Flask on the step, flask on the step
Wake up slow, I'm coming home to you
Sugar and steam and a drive safe, love
Flask on the step, that's all I need

[Outro - sax riff, tambourine fade]
Flask on the step, flask on the step
Thank you, darling, thank you for the tea

tracks.title: The Tent Has Been to Wales
tracks.genre: 70s UK soft-rock with sax hook (10cc and Gerry Rafferty lineage)
tracks.subject: a man who lent his two-man tent to a friend, who lent it to a cousin, and it has now slept nine strangers across three countries while he has never used it
tracks.caption: 70s UK soft-rock with a sax hook, glossy AM-radio studio production. Chorus-pedal clean electric guitar arpeggios, Fender Rhodes electric piano, melodic fretless bass, alto saxophone hook in the choruses, light congas and a tight snare. Warm analog compression, layered harmony vocals on the chorus. Male lead, smooth light baritone, wry deadpan delivery that stays clearly sung. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 112 BPM, E major. Breezy, good-humoured mood. No rap, no autotune, no heavy distortion, no synth bass, no drum machine.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - chorus-pedal guitar, Rhodes, light congas]

[Verse 1]
I lent my tent to Dave in June
He said he'd have it back by noon
Dave gave it to his cousin Jo
Jo took it where the sheep all go

[Pre-Chorus]
A postcard came from Aberystwyth
Wish you were here, it said, and sorry

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
It's been to Wales without me
Nine people slept inside it
And not one of them was me

[Verse 2]
A man named Piet in Rotterdam
Has patched it up with duct tape and jam
A girl in Cork I've never met
Sent me a photo of it wet

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
It's been to Rotterdam and Cork
Nine people slept inside it
I just wanted one night in it

[Bridge - guitar alone, then congas]
I only asked to borrow it back
Dave says Friday, it's on the motorway

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
And now it's coming home to me
Ten people will have slept inside it
And it's me, I'm the tenth, finally

[Outro - sax and guitar trade lines, fade]
The tent has been to Wales
Pitch it in the garden, I'll be fine

tracks.title: Monday After Closing
tracks.genre: Dunedin-sound jangle-pop (New Zealand lo-fi 1980s lineage)
tracks.subject: a woman who winds the eleven antique clocks in a small city museum every Monday after closing, and the one clock she leaves stopped at ten past four on purpose
tracks.caption: Dunedin-sound jangle-pop, New Zealand 1980s lo-fi lineage. Two jangling twelve-string-style electric guitars in bright open chords, trebly melodic bass, shuffling snare-and-tom drums, tambourine and a short organ drone in the chorus. Four-track room sound with light tape hiss, unpolished and close. Female lead, plain light alto, slightly ragged but clearly sung, a friend doubling the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 138 BPM, D major. Bright, wistful mood. No synth, no autotune, no big reverb wash, no distorted fuzz, no drum machine.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - jangling guitars, tambourine]

[Verse 1]
Monday after the doors are locked
I take the keys and I take the stairs
Eleven clocks in the Long Gallery
Ten brass keys on a loop of string

[Pre-Chorus]
One by one I turn them round
Listen for the tick to settle down

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
All the others keep on going
That one stays behind

[Verse 2]
The guard goes home at half past six
The radiator knocks and ticks
The oak one always strikes too late
The tall one swears it's half past eight

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
All the others keep on going
That one stays behind

[Bridge - guitars drop to a single strum]
The curator asked me to fix it
That was three years of Mondays ago

[Chorus]
Ten past four, ten past four
That one I never wind
Everybody's racing round the room
It's the one that stays behind

[Outro - jangle fade, tambourine]
Ten past four, ten past four
Lock the door, I'll be back next Monday

tracks.genre: upright-piano saloon torch ballad (1950s late-night lounge)
tracks.subject: a woman who still has the jazz record a man lent her eleven years ago and has never returned it, because as long as she has it he has a reason to call
tracks.caption: 1950s late-night lounge torch ballad in slow 6/8. Upright piano with slightly honky tone and sustained chords, brushed snare, upright bass walking gently, muted trumpet answering the vocal and a distant cello in the last chorus. Close-miked small-club room with soft tape saturation. Female lead, low alto, slow and fully sung with sustained notes. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 66 BPM, F major. Hushed, rueful, tender mood. No drum machine, no electric guitar, no synth, no autotune, no dance beat.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - upright piano, brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
You lent me a record on a Friday night
Said bring it back Friday, I'll leave on the light
The sleeve has gone soft where my thumb goes
The needle still finds it with its eyes closed

[Pre-Chorus]
I've moved four times and it came with me
In a box marked kitchen, so nobody sees

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
I could post it in a minute
Then you'd have no cause to call

[Verse 2]
A woman at the shop said just sell it, dear
It's worth some money, it's scratched, it's rare
I said I know what it's worth to me
It's the only Friday I keep

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
I could post it in a minute
Then you'd have no cause to call

[Bridge - piano alone, trumpet enters]
If you ask me for it back
I'll say I lost it, come and look

[Chorus]
Side B, eleven years
Still waiting on your call
Come and get it, come and get it
Come and take the record back

[Outro - piano and muted trumpet, slow fade]
Bring it back Friday
I'll leave on the light

tracks.title: Back Pew at Half Past Five
tracks.genre: synth-folk (Nordic-style)
tracks.subject: a Finnish church verger who unlocks the church at half past five every winter morning, and the one stranger who always sits in the back pew for ten minutes and never speaks
tracks.caption: Nordic-style synth-folk. Warm analog synth pads, fingerpicked nylon acoustic guitar, plucked kantele on the melody, soft electronic pulse and low harmonium drone. Spacious cold-room reverb, analog warmth and slight tape wobble on the pads. Female lead, clear light mezzo-soprano, steady and clearly sung with close harmony on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, D minor. Hushed, patient, gently warm mood. No trap beats, no autotune, no dance drops, no distorted guitar, no big orchestral strings.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - fingerpicked guitar, synth pad, kantele]

[Verse 1]
Half past five and the snow's still blue
I find the right key on the ring
Turn on one lamp and the radiator
Wake the old boards with my boots

[Pre-Chorus]
Eleven degrees inside the porch
I breathe on my hands and I wait

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
You take the back pew by the door
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Verse 2]
I don't know your name or your trade
Your boots are the colour of salt
Some mornings you stay for the whole bell
Some mornings you don't take your hat off

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
You take the back pew by the door
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Bridge - guitar and kantele only]
Today the pew was empty
I kept the lamp on anyway

[Chorus]
You come in with the cold on your coat
I hear the door, I don't turn round
Ten minutes, never a word
I leave the lamp on for you

[Outro - synth pad, kantele, fade]
Half past five and the snow's still blue
The lamp is on

tracks.genre: Showa nagashi-style kayokyoku (Shinjuku wandering-guitarist ballad)
tracks.subject: a convenience-store night clerk and the last wandering nagashi guitarist, who buys one canned coffee at 2 a.m. and pays for it by playing the two-note door chime as a song
tracks.caption: Showa nagashi-style kayokyoku, Shinjuku wandering-guitarist ballad. Nylon-string guitar fingerpicked with a slow arpeggio, accordion holding long sustained chords, upright bass walking gently, brushed snare on the backbeat. Dry 1970s studio sound, tape warmth, light plate reverb. Male baritone, mid-low register, clearly sung ballad melody with a slight kobushi at phrase ends. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 72 BPM, A minor. Wistful, warm, late-night mood. No electronic drums, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no distorted guitar, no pop synth pads.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - nylon guitar and accordion]
[Verse 1]
午前二時の コンビニの前
ギターを背負った 爺さんが
缶コーヒーを ひとつだけ
毎晩おなじ 時間に買う
[Pre-Chorus]
レジに立つ僕に 笑って言った
流しの仕事は もうないんだと
[Chorus]
リクエストは 何かあるかい
ドアが開くたび 鳴るあの音を
ピンポンと鳴る 二つの音を
爺さんの指が 歌にする
[Verse 2]
朝まで続く 長い夜勤
僕の仕事は 弁当を並べる
爺さんの膝で 弦が鳴ると
冷たい棚が 少しあったかい
[Pre-Chorus]
客が来ない 三時過ぎ
店の中に 昭和が流れる
[Chorus]
リクエストは 何かあるかい
ドアが開くたび 鳴るあの音を
ピンポンと鳴る 二つの音を
今夜は僕が 口ずさむ
[Bridge - accordion alone]
缶コーヒーの 代わりに
一曲 おごらせてくれ
[Chorus]
ありがとうと 言う代わりに
ドアが開くたび 鳴るあの音を
ピンポンと鳴る 二つの音を
始発が来るまで 弾いている
[Outro - nylon guitar fades]

tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - mellotron and 7/8 guitar riff]
[Verse 1]
文化祭は 五時で終わった
たこ焼きの屋台は 全部売り切れ
鉄板のふたの 下にだけ
最後の一パックが 隠れてる
[Pre-Chorus]
受付で 券をちぎってた子は
まだ机を 片づけてる

手のひらだけが 汗をかく
七つ数える 足音のたび

三百八十枚の 入場券を

廊下の端で 椅子を引く音
きみが こっちを向いた

冷めないうちに 渡せたらいい
今度は足が 先に出る
七つ数えて 声を出す
最後の一個 きみの分

青のりが 歯につくよと
笑われても いいから
[Chorus]
冷めたたこ焼き ふたりで分けた
ソースの匂いの 帰り道
七つ数えず 歩きだす
[Outro - 7/8 riff slowly unwinds]

tracks.title: 梨をかぐ人
tracks.genre: Japanese 1970s southern soul with horn section (Memphis-style, upbeat)
tracks.subject: a shotengai greengrocer whose regular Mrs. Ogawa has sniffed one pear every day for six years without buying, until the day she asks for two
tracks.caption: Japanese 1970s southern soul in the Memphis style, upbeat and danceable. Hammond organ with Leslie swell, punchy electric bass on the one, tenor sax and trumpet playing short horn stabs, tight live drums with a hard snare, chicken-scratch electric guitar. 1970s analog studio sound, spring reverb, tape saturation. Male tenor, gritty but clearly sung, with short gang backing vocals answering each hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 112 BPM, G major. Cheeky, upbeat, warm mood. No autotune, no trap hi-hats, no EDM synths, no rapped verses, no modern pop gloss.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - horn stabs and Hammond organ]
[Verse 1]
商店街の 八百屋の店先
おかみさんが 毎日来る
梨をひとつ 手に取って
鼻に近づけ すんすんと嗅ぐ
[Pre-Chorus]
六年間 毎日嗅いで
一個も買わない
[Chorus]
嗅ぐだけじゃ 梨は 買えないよ
ヘイ おかみさん 財布を出して
今日の梨は 水がたれる
嗅ぐだけ嗅いで 帰らないで
[Verse 2]
親父の俺は 声をからして
今日もタイムセール 叫んでる
でもあの人の 鼻だけは
一番正直な 値札だった
[Pre-Chorus]
ある日おかみさんが 言った
今日はね 買うわ 二つ
[Chorus]
嗅ぐだけでなく 買ってくれたら
ヘイ おかみさん 袋は二重
今日の梨は おまけ付き
嗅ぐ人来ないと 店が淋しい
[Bridge - horns and handclaps]
六年分の おつりだよ
おまけにもう一個 持ってけ
[Chorus]
嗅いで 買って 笑ってる
ヘイ みんな 梨を嗅いでおいで
明日の梨も 水がたれる
嗅ぐだけでいい 来てくれたら
[Outro - horn stabs and organ fade]

tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - ukulele strum and glockenspiel]
[Verse 1]
新婚三日目の 日曜の朝
ミョウガ買ってきて と頼まれた
商店街の 八百屋の前
ミョウガはどれだ 立ちつくす
[Pre-Chorus]
ネギじゃない 生姜じゃない
紫の小さな 何かだ
[Chorus]
八百屋のおじさん 教えてよ
ミョウガの季節は 夏の終わり
かごに入れたら ほら笑顔
奥さんの待つ 家まで走る
[Verse 2]
おじさんは 袋に三つ詰めて
奥さん 目が高いねと言って
茄子も一本 おまけして
秋はじめの 香りがした
[Pre-Chorus]
玄関で 袋を差し出したら
正解よ と 笑われた
[Chorus]
八百屋のおじさん ありがとう
ミョウガの季節は 夏の終わり
そうめんの上に ほら笑顔
二人で食べる 日曜の昼
[Bridge - ukulele and glockenspiel]
来年も 買いに行くよ
今度は 迷わずに
[Chorus]
八百屋のおじさん また来るよ
ミョウガの季節は 夏の終わり
かごに入れたら ほら笑顔
奥さんの待つ 家まで歩く
[Outro - ukulele and glockenspiel end]

tracks.subject: a girl who carries cuttings of her grandmother's rau răm and basil in cut plastic bottles to her sixth-floor apartment balcony and phones grandma every morning to report the leaf count

tracks.caption: Hanoi xẩm street-busker folk in a brisk playful tempo. tracks.caption: Vietnamese flamenco-pop in rumba flamenca style. Nylon-string flamenca guitar playing quick rasgueado strums and light picado runs, palmas hand claps on the offbeats, cajon with a firm bass tone and a snappy slap, round acoustic bass, solo violin answering the vocal on the chorus. Dry intimate studio sound with natural room reverb and close-miked strings. Female warm low-mid voice, sung close and smiling. No electronic drums, no synth bass, no autotune, no rap, no heavy distortion.

Anh chạy tới sạp may, mồ hôi trên trán

tracks.title: 熱奶茶，走甜

tracks.subject: a cha chaan teng waiter who has written the same order slip for a regular at table seven for three years without a word between them, until she orders in his kitchen shorthand and adds one more item
tracks.caption: 1980s Cantopop synth power ballad, gated-drum Hong Kong TV-theme style.
